requirements.text: Find her most recent resolved incident and reopen it so the team can investigate further.
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM incident WHERE incident_id = 'INC_022' AND status = 'in_progress' AND caller_id = 'USER_010'
assumptions: Isabella Rossi is USER_010; her resolved incidents are INC_011 (VPN, resolved 2024-02-22 12:00) and INC_022 (Email sync issues on mobile device, resolved 2024-02-26 15:20), so the most recent, and the email sync one, is INC_022
reopen means status in_progress: the policy allows resolved to move only to closed or in_progress
caller_id = USER_010 kept from the benchmark check; it holds on the seed and pins the incident to Isabella Rossi

requirements.text: Send a notification to the agent who originally resolved it (subject: 'Reopened Incident: Further Action Required on Your Previous Resolution') explaining that the issue has recurred and asking them to try a different approach this time

cells.subject: Reopened Incident: Further Action Required on Your Previous Resolution

requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM notification WHERE notification_id = 'NOTIF_008' AND incident_id = 'INC_022' AND email = 'kenji.tanaka@acme.com' AND type = 'report' AND subject = 'Reopened Incident: Further Action Required on Your Previous Resolution' AND message LIKE '%kenji tanaka%' AND message LIKE '%thank%' AND message LIKE '%previous%' AND message LIKE '%email sync%' AND message LIKE '%reconfiguration%' AND message LIKE '%isabella rossi%' AND message LIKE '%approach%' AND message LIKE '%different%' AND message LIKE '%resolve%' AND message LIKE '%daily task%' AND message LIKE '%disruption%'
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (NOTIF_007 is the highest notification id in the seed)
the agent who resolved INC_022 is its resolved_by, Kenji Tanaka (USER_009, kenji.tanaka@acme.com), an active agent
type report kept from the benchmark check; not fixed by request or policy
greet by full name gives 'kenji tanaka'; thank for previous work gives 'thank' and 'previous'; what the incident was about gives 'email sync' (its short description)
what they did to resolve it gives 'reconfiguration' and 'resolve', from INC_022's resolution notes 'Email sync working correctly after reconfiguration'
a different approach gives 'different' and 'approach'; the permanent-fix sentence gives 'isabella rossi', 'daily task' and 'disruption'
the benchmark's LOWER(message) is written as message LIKE, which ignores ASCII case in SQLite, so the test is unchanged

requirements.text: Find her most recent resolved incident
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM incident WHERE incident_id = 'INC_011' AND status = 'resolved'
assumptions: boundary of 'most recent resolved incident': INC_011 (VPN connection failure, resolved 2024-02-22) is Isabella Rossi's other resolved incident, older and not about email sync, so it is not reopened

notes: The acting user, Raj Patel (USER_007), is an admin in ORG_002, Isabella Rossi's organisation, so the reopen and the notification are permitted. 'Explaining that the issue has recurred' is not tested as a message term: the benchmark does not test it and the request fixes no wording for it ('happening again', 'recurred' and 'back' would all serve). The term 'reconfiguration' comes from INC_022's resolution notes; the work notes instead say 'Mobile device configuration updated', so a message that paraphrases the work notes would miss it, but the resolution notes are the record of what the agent did to resolve it. INC_013 (Unable to access email) is closed, not resolved, and the policy has no transition out of closed, so it needs no separate stay. Reopening does not require clearing resolved_by, resolution_code or resolution_notes; neither the request nor the policy says so, so those cells are not tested. The notification's org_id and status are not fixed by the request or policy. The two independent passes agreed on every requirement, cell, value and disposition; there were no disagreements to resolve.
